cards.text: This is a prayer from David, the shepherd who became Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), written when he was in the cave. And friend, he is NOT whispering in there. He cries aloud and lifts his voice to the LORD.

cards.question: David lifts his voice to the LORD from that cave. What is he asking for?

cards.text: Then he pours out his complaint before the LORD. Not one tidy sentence. The WHOLE thing, like when you ask a friend 'How are you?' and they give you twenty minutes, and honestly? I respect it.

cards.question: True or false: David keeps his trouble to himself and hides it from the LORD.

cards.text: David admits his spirit grows faint within him. Phone-at-2% faint. And with that last little bit of battery, he tells the LORD one thing.

cards.question: True or false: Even as his spirit grows faint, David tells the LORD that He knows David's way.

cards.text: Then David talks about the path he travels. Somebody has hidden something along it, and I promise you, baker, it is NOT a welcome mat.

cards.question: What has been hidden along the path David travels?

cards.text: Next, David asks the LORD to look to his right and see.

cards.question: When the LORD looks to David's right, what does David say is there?
True or false: Looking around, David says there is no refuge for him and no one cares for his soul.

cards.text: Nobody at his right hand. Baker, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and the only one next to me was a twist tie... who did NOT have my back. So David turns and cries out to the LORD.

cards.question: With no refuge anywhere around him, David tells the LORD that He is his ___.

cards.text: Then David asks the LORD to listen to his cry, because he's been brought quite low. He's got people chasing him, and he asks to be rescued from them.

cards.question: David asks to be rescued from his pursuers because they are too ___ for him.

cards.text: Last line of the prayer. David reaches for one more picture of where his soul is stuck.

cards.question: What does David ask the LORD to free his soul from?
David wants his soul set free so that he may ___ the LORD's name.
The man with nobody at his right hand pictures people gathering around him. Who does David say will gather?
True or false: David says the righteous will gather around him because of his own courage.

findings.problem: Card 1 calls David 'the shepherd who became Israel's king' and cites 2 Samuel 5:3. That verse supports only the king part. The shepherd fact has no reference of its own.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Card 3 says David pours out his whole complaint before the LORD. That gives away card 4, the true or false question on whether David hides his trouble from the LORD.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 3 has four sentences: 'Then he pours out…', 'Not one tidy sentence.', 'The WHOLE thing… honestly?' and 'I respect it.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 5 has three sentences: 'David admits…', 'Phone-at-2% faint.' and 'And with that last little bit of battery…'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 12 has three sentences, carries more than two beats (a recap of verse 4, the drawer joke, and the turn to verse 5), and opens by recapping 'Nobody at his right hand,' which cards 10 and 11 already covered.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke adds new drawer facts: a twist tie was 'the only one next to me', and it 'did NOT have my back.' The backstory says many friends were in the drawer and 'They were all in it together.' The line also holds a grudge against a drawer friend.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Card 13's question says 'With no refuge anywhere around him,' and card 11 just used 'no refuge.' That repeated wording points straight to 'refuge' and gives the answer away instead of letting the baker reason it out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: No card mentions the second half of Psalm 142:5, where David calls the LORD 'my portion in the land of the living.' The baker leaves without this key line of David's confession.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
